requirements.statement: Open with a Summary section: one paragraph on who, what, where, and the decision.
Then a Facts section. Every fact cites the document in the file it comes from, in square brackets: [notice of loss], [police report], [invoice 1].

source: const ok = brs.length > 0 && brs.every(b => names.some(n => n === b || n.startsWith(b) || b.startsWith(n)));
bad.push({ start: Math.max(idx, 0), end: Math.max(idx, 0) + s.length, why: 'fact without a cited document in the file' });
return { ok: bad.length === 0, detail: bad.length ? bad.length + ' uncited or unmatched fact(s)' : 'every fact cites a document in the file', spans: bad };
means: Every sentence in the Facts section carries a bracketed document name that matches a document in the material.

requirements.statement: Then a Coverage analysis section. The coverage conclusion cites the policy clause it rests on, and every exclusion that could apply is addressed and cited.

means: The Coverage analysis cites a policy clause number and cites the policy document; the exclusions that could apply are addressed in the text. Whether every applicable exclusion is found is judgement.

requirements.statement: Then a Decision section: covered or not covered, and under which clause.
End with a Reserve section. The reserve equals the sum of the invoices in the file, less any excess the schedule applies, and cites the invoices.

source: (text, request, material) => { const m = text.match(/(^|\n)##\s*Reserve\s*\n([\s\S]*?)$/i); if (!m) return null; const body = m[2]; const invs = material.filter(x => /invoice/i.test(x.name)); let total = 0; for (const inv of invs) { const amts = [...inv.text.matchAll(/\$?\s?([\d]{1,3}(?:,\d{3})*(?:\.\d{2})?)/g)].map(x => parseFloat(x[1].replace(/,/g,''))); const totals = inv.text.match(/total[^\d]*([\d,]+(?:\.\d+)?)/i); total += totals ? parseFloat(totals[1].replace(/,/g,'')) : (amts.length ? Math.max(...amts) : 0); } const figs = [...body.matchAll(/([\d]{1,3}(?:,\d{3})+|\d+)(?:\.\d+)?\s*(dollars|\$)?/gi)].map(x => parseFloat(x[1].replace(/,/g,''))); const ok = total > 0 && figs.includes(total) && /\[[^\]]*invoice[^\]]*\]/i.test(body); return { ok, detail: ok ? 'reserve matches invoice sum and cites invoices' : 'reserve does not match invoice sum or lacks invoice citations (expected ' + total + ')', spans: ok ? [] : [{start: text.indexOf(body), end: text.indexOf(body)+body.length, why: 'reserve check failed'}] }; }
means: The Reserve section's figure equals the sum of the invoice amounts found in the material, and the section cites the invoices; the Reserve section is the last section.

requirements.statement: Never speculate about the insured's intent or honesty.

source: (text) => { const re = /\b(intend(?:ed|s)?|intent|motive|deliberate(?:ly)?|honest(?:y)?|dishonest|lying|lied|staged|pretend(?:ed)?|wanted to)\b/gi; const spans=[]; let m; while((m=re.exec(text))){ spans.push({start:m.index,end:m.index+m[0].length,why:'speculation on insured intent or honesty'}); } return { ok: spans.length===0, detail: spans.length ? spans.length+' speculative term(s)' : 'no speculation on intent or honesty', spans }; }
means: No sentence attributes intent, honesty or motive to the insured.

requirements.statement: Every figure in the work is one the request or the material gives.
I keep paragraphs to 5 sentences at most.
I hedge rarely: at most 2 hedging words per thousand.
The Summary section runs 25 to 33 words in my pieces.
The Facts section runs 47 to 65 words in my pieces.

Write none of the moves that mark text as machine-written (announcing an insight others "miss", grading your own list, "the single most", announcing candour, "that's the whole game", reading the reader's mind, one thing "wearing another's clothes", a contrastive verdict as the opening line, an em dash, a run of three or more very short sentences).
No mechanical errors: spelling, agreement, punctuation.
